references.text: Describes the principle that a close relative (goel) shall redeem a brother who has become poor and sold his property.
The preceding verse setting the context for an Israelite who has sold himself to a foreigner.
Continues the list of relatives who may redeem, including uncle or cousin.
Boaz acts as redeemer (goel) for Ruth and Naomi, demonstrating the principle of the kinsman's right of redemption in practice.
The Lord declares Himself as Israel's goel (redeemer), who redeems His people.
God has redeemed Israel from their sins, a spiritual application of the goel principle.
Jeremiah exercises his right of redemption as a close relative by buying a field from his cousin Hanamel.
Christ gave Himself to redeem us from all lawlessness, as the ultimate goel.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, fulfilling the role of redeemer.
God sent His Son to redeem those who were under the law.
We are redeemed with Christ's precious blood, not with perishable things like silver or gold.
